themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover — Still the Read
themes.narrative: The tape reads like an AI unwind becoming a broad rollover: the Mag 7 sit on average 16% below their 52-week highs while the index holds near its own.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 2.8% below its 52-week high against the Mag 7 average of -16%, a 13.2-point divergence gap; AAPL is the strongest Mag 7 name at -0.1% from its high while NVDA is the weakest at -28.6%. Credit is not confirming a rollover: bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.34, calm. The index is rotating leadership, not breaking.
themes.counterRead: The divergence itself is the risk: concentration this wide means the index can look fine while the names that drove it keep falling. If credit flips — HY OAS above 4% or lending standards tightening — the rotation read dies and the rollover read takes over. Until then, index-level calm is real, not a mask.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% or SLOOS moving toward the stress zone; Mag 7 average distance from highs narrowing back under 10 points.

themes.label: AI Bounce, Not a Bottom — Yet
themes.narrative: SMH +4.82% and NVDA +2.87% today are being read as the bottom in for the AI complex after a -30.02% month for NVDA.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA closed at 173.73, below the $175 Zone 2 floor for a second straight close (Nov 10: 168.89) — the Nov 9 suspected bottom stays voided. SMH closed at 506.96, just $1.96 above the Zone 2 ceiling, still -24.54% from its high and -9.81% below its 50-day. The mechanical tally is only 2 of 4: VIX rollover and credit calm confirm, but zone occupancy and the volume-climax signal do not (SMH volume 1.22x its 20-day average, close in 53% of its range).
themes.counterRead: The bounce without a close inside Zone 2 is the pivot-and-fail shape, not a confirmed turn. The real opportunity is underneath it — NVDA revenue growing 61.4% YoY with the stock -28% from its high and RSI at 30.2 — but it only becomes actionable on a confirming close back inside Zone 2, not on the bounce itself.
themes.watchFor: NVDA close vs the $175 Zone 2 floor; SMH close vs the $470 floor and $505 ceiling; tally moving to 3 of 4.

themes.label: Software: Fundamentals Ahead of Price
themes.narrative: Software is priced as dead money after the AI unwind: NOW -25.9% in a month, DDOG -34.4%, HUBS -50.6% from its high, RDDT -60% from its high.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG scores 82 (tier A): revenue growing 27.7% YoY, 80% gross margin, FCF $1,001M at a 29.2% margin, while the stock sits -38.2% below its high at RSI 32.2. AVGO scores 81 (tier A): revenue growing 55% YoY, -29.5% below its high. ONTO scores 79: revenue growing 41.5% YoY, -44% below its high. NOW sits -41.3% from its high at RSI 30.9. All four declines are flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental.
themes.counterRead: The divergence between revenue growth and price is the opportunity, but there is no near-term catalyst: DDOG and ONTO have no earnings before Jan 13, and AVGO reports Dec 9. Size on closes that hold, not on the bounce — a sentiment-driven dislocation can stay dislocated until a print forces the re-rate.
themes.watchFor: DDOG and AVGO closes holding above current levels; AVGO earnings Dec 9; any insider or guidance signal that breaks the sentiment read.

themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power: Trough Buyers Are Insiders
themes.narrative: Nuclear and AI-power names unwound with AI: CCJ -14.45% in a month, OKLO -19.76%, SMR -19.88%, GEV -20.31%, VST -19.32%.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the top conviction promotion at score 83: $134.892, -28.7% from its peak, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, revenue growing 19.1% YoY, P/S 2.6x. BWXT scores 77 (tier B): -47.9% from its high, revenue growing 18.3% YoY. NXT leads the one-month board at +13.3%, showing the complex is differentiating, not uniformly dying.
themes.counterRead: Contracted cash flow (VST, BWXT) is separating from the pre-revenue story, and the trough buyers are insiders, not the tape. But VST carries an ACUTE_CATALYST flag — understand the catalyst before acting — and the bounce needs a close above the recent range to confirm. The insider signal is the edge; the tape has not confirmed it yet.
themes.watchFor: VST close vs the $134.89 level and any insider follow-through; CCJ and OKLO closes for complex confirmation.

themes.label: Rates Elevated, Credit Calm — The Falsifier Has Not Fired
themes.narrative: Hot CPI Oct (active event, HIGH signal strength) killed rate-cut hopes, and the market is pricing supersized-hike risk — the kind of print that should be breaking credit.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 4.88%, below the 5.2% falsifier line; the 2s10s curve is +0.32, not inverted; HY OAS is 3.34, calm and not cracking; the fed funds rate is 3.88%. The damage is running through duration and the AI unwind, not through credit.
themes.counterRead: Calm credit is what keeps the rotation read alive — but it is a condition, not a guarantee. If HY OAS crosses 4% or the 10-year crosses 5.2%, the calm read dies, the stand-down triggers, and the Tranche A re-arm path closes. The next reads are FOMC minutes Nov 18 (watch) and PCE Oct Nov 25 (watch).
themes.watchFor: 10-year vs the 5.2% falsifier; HY OAS vs 4%; FOMC minutes Nov 18.

strategyPosture: Watch. The bounce is sharp — SPX +1.31%, SMH +4.82%, VIX down 10.12% to 17.49 — but it is unconfirmed: NVDA closed at 173.73, still below the $175 Zone 2 floor, and the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4. TQQQ is -25.23% over the month. Hold cash; no probe until a close confirms.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move is decided at two lines: NVDA's $175 Zone 2 floor and the SPX 7,750-7,820 failure zone. A NVDA close back inside Zone 2 with SMH holding $470 re-arms the Tranche A probe; a bounce that stalls and rolls over at the failure zone confirms the trap and keeps the ladder on the sidelines.

SMH close vs the $470 Zone 2 floor and $505 ceiling (closed 506.96, just above the ceiling)
SPX close vs the 7,750-7,820 failure zone and vs the 200-day at 7,334.28

reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 11 close: SPX 7,619.38, -2.87% from its 120-day high and -0.69% below its 50-day but +3.89% above its 200-day; SMH 506.96 BETWEEN_ZONES (just above the $470-505 Zone 2 ceiling), -24.54% from its high; NVDA 173.73 BELOW_ZONE_2, -28.61% from its high and -19.99% below its 50-day; VIX 17.49 rolling over from a 28.18 five-day high; HY OAS 3.34 calm; mechanical tally 2 of 4.

ladder.trigger: NVDA closes back inside Zone 2 ($175-185) AND SMH closes holding Zone 2 ($470-505) with VIX below 25 and the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better
ladder.response: Re-arm Tranche A per the deployment ladder: starter probe sized to the ladder, SMH limit $505, no chasing above the zone

ladder.trigger: SPX closes into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone or SMH into 580-600, then rolls over and closes back below the zone
ladder.response: Treat as the bull trap: do not chase the bounce, cut any probe entered on it, stay in Watch with cash

ladder.trigger: SMH closes below the $470 Zone 2 floor, or NVDA closes below $168.89 (the Nov 10 low close)
ladder.response: Tranche A stays void; no probe at the next leg down until zones are re-mapped — the correction is escalating, not bottoming

ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4%, or VIX closes above 25, or SPX closes below its 200-day at 7,334.28
ladder.response: Stand down: regime-break conditions met, Tranche A re-arm is off the table and the ladder is suspended pending a fresh regime read

ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds with the 10-year falling, or SPX closes above 7,820 with SMH above 600
ladder.response: Confirmed-bottom conditions for Tranche C: re-audit zones and ratios before deploying the 50% tranche — no auto-deployment

reaction.invalidation: SPX closes above 7,820 with SMH above 600 and VIX holding below 17 — the correction is over, the Watch stance was too cautious, and the ladder's trap framing is void. Conversely, SPX closing below the 200-day at 7,334.28 proves the correction is deepening into a regime break and voids the Tranche A re-arm path entirely.
reaction.trapRisk: Today's bounce is exactly the pivot-and-fail shape: SMH +4.82% and NVDA +2.87%, but NVDA's close of 173.73 is still below the $175 floor, SMH sits only $1.96 above the Zone 2 ceiling, and the live QQQ quote at assembly (684.6, +1.46% on the day) already faded from the session's strength. Do not chase the first bounce and do not size on intraday prices — entries wait for a close back inside Zone 2, and any probe taken on the bounce is cut if SPX rejects the 7,750-7,820 failure zone.
